slice.candidate: authorized Git-only protocol: immutable checkpoint + CAS LATEST + immutable own receipt + exact readback
slice.scope: role-local GitHub transport semantics plus current cross_field LATEST only; no public web and no O/downstream/other-worker/legacy semantics

stale_state_detection.evidence: LATEST replacement requires the exact current blob SHA. A writer holding an older LATEST SHA cannot silently overwrite a newer pointer; the write conflicts instead.

duplicate_effect_resistance.evidence: Checkpoint and receipt paths are immutable create-only artifacts, while the sole commit point is the CAS replacement of LATEST. Two writers starting from the same predecessor may create distinct orphan artifacts, but they cannot both successfully advance that same predecessor pointer. Duplicate committed pointer effects are therefore excluded at this protocol layer.

interrupted_run_recovery.evidence: Interruption before checkpoint creation leaves no effect; interruption after checkpoint creation but before the LATEST CAS leaves only an immutable orphan and preserves the prior authoritative LATEST; interruption after a successful LATEST CAS leaves the new checkpoint reconstructible even if the immutable receipt has not yet been written. The first two cases are safe by write ordering/API preconditions and the third is reconstructible from LATEST, but this role has not yet injected an interruption between checkpoint creation and LATEST CAS and read back the unchanged pointer in a dedicated test.

restart_reconstruction.evidence: The protocol records exact checkpoint path/blob in LATEST and requires exact readback. A later invocation can reconstruct the authoritative role-local state from LATEST without relying on commit messages, diffs, other roles, or legacy state. This r237 transaction is itself persisted using that structure and will be exact-read back before return.

slice.commit_semantics: Successful CAS update of research_workers_clean_g1/cross_field/LATEST.json is the unique authoritative pointer-advance event; immutable checkpoint/receipt files created without that CAS are non-authoritative orphans.
slice.quota_assessment: The protocol uses only lightweight repository transport and does not require hosted runners, Codespaces, artifacts/LFS, packages, cloud compute/storage credits, external model/API execution, or manual user execution. Rate limiting remains a cross-invocation transport condition, not an accepted finite monthly quota dependency.

conflict_check: Used only current sanitized controls, exact identity-only transport for the manifest-required control set, own cross_field LATEST, and the authorized role-local GitHub write surface. Unrelated control semantics were not consumed. No scheduler mutation, O/protected authority, downstream state, other-worker state, other-role receipts, shared ledger, or legacy research contributed to the slice.
frontier: Keep provider-independent append-only persistence unresolved; the Git-only route is not provider-independent acceptance evidence.

Fault-inject exactly the checkpoint-created/LATEST-not-updated interruption state using one deliberately non-authoritative orphan checkpoint, then verify by exact readback that LATEST remains on its prior blob and the next bootstrap ignores the orphan.
After that bounded interruption test, audit the post-LATEST/pre-receipt interruption case only if still needed; do not start it in the same invocation.
exact_continuation: Fresh-bootstrap current controls and reconstruct r237 from LATEST. Execute exactly one bounded Phase-1 leaf that fault-injects the checkpoint-created/LATEST-not-updated interruption case on the authorized Git-only protocol: create one explicitly non-authoritative role-local orphan test checkpoint whose content names the current LATEST blob, intentionally do not update LATEST to it, then exact-read LATEST once and verify its blob/content are unchanged. Persist the test outcome and nonempty continuation. Do not test a second interruption stage in the same invocation, do not mutate scheduler state, and keep provider-independent persistence unresolved.
